               <ns0:p n="1">1 LET us therefore fear <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">The Spirit draws this Counsel from the former sad event of Unbelief in the Progenitors of these <ns0:hi>Hebrews,</ns0:hi> who were shut out of an Earthly <ns0:hi>Canaan</ns0:hi> by it, which was pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mised to them: Hereon he adviseth them to avoid that Sin which will have now as fearful a Punishment, <ns0:hi>viz.</ns0:hi> the shutting them out of the Heavenly <ns0:hi>Canaan,</ns0:hi> tendred and promised to Believers in the Gospel. <ns0:hi>Fear</ns0:hi> is that affecti<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />on of the Soul, by which it avoideth and shunneth what is hurtful to it, and here carrieth in it a gracious and Child<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />like care and jealousy of slighting the Father's Promise, and coming short of Heaven; it is a Fear issuing from Faith, <ns0:hi>Phil.</ns0:hi> 2.12.</ns0:note>, lest a promise being left <ns0:hi>us</ns0:hi> 
                  <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">Lest the Promise of God to Men, who sware some should not enter, but promised others should, as <ns0:hi>Numb.</ns0:hi> 14.23, 24, 30, 31. A Promise of the most Excel<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lent, Glorious and Heavenly Rest made to Believers, <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 11.10. This was graciously <ns0:hi>left</ns0:hi> or made to them by God, but <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> here is an <ns0:hi>act of Sin, lest we by Sin should leave or reject God's Promise</ns0:hi> of the better, as the <ns0:hi>Hebrews</ns0:hi> did of the literal Rest by their Unbelief and Disobedience to God's Law, and so is the proper object of Fear, and there<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fore ought to have been read, <ns0:hi>lest the Promise being left be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />hind.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>, of entring into his rest <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">Of a free entrance into Heaven, and enjoying a glorious Rest with God there.</ns0:note>, any of you should seem to come short of it <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">He would have it the Fear of all, that not <ns0:hi>one Soul</ns0:hi> might be indangered by it; so as not in any measure to slight such a Promise, nor as much as to seem so, flying from the very appearance of Evil, 1 <ns0:hi>Thess.</ns0:hi> 5.12. <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>, a Metaphor taken from <ns0:hi>Racers, where any are out-run and left behind,</ns0:hi> noting the mi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />serable state of such Christians who profess to run to Heaven, but never do so as to obtain it, 1 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 9.24, 25, 26. Alas, He that falleth short of Heaven, reacheth home to Hell.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="2">2 For unto us was the Gospel preached as well as unto them <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">The reason inforcing the former counsel is, their ha<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ving mutually the same means, the one as the other, and if they fear not, may be guilty of the same Sin; for the <ns0:hi>Hebrews</ns0:hi> and the whole Chrcuh were <ns0:hi>Evangelized</ns0:hi> by the outward publishing to them, and their professed recepti<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />on of the glad tidings of Salvation by God the Son incar<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nate, who was to lead them in the way to God's Eter<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nal Rest; which if they had been truly Evangelized and transformed by, they could never have been shut out of God's Rest. The same Gospel being preached to both their fore-Fathers and them, though more gloriously revealed to the latter, 2 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 3.10, 11. For the Gospel was preach<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed to <ns0:hi>Abraham</ns0:hi> and to his Off-spring, that in his eminent Seed, the Lord Jesus Christ, all Nations should be blessed, <ns0:hi>Gen.</ns0:hi> 22.18. compare <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> 8.56. He was the Angel of the Covenant that was Lord of God's Hosts, and was to lead them into the Literal and Heavenly <ns0:hi>Canaan, Exod.</ns0:hi> 23.20. <ns0:hi>Iosh.</ns0:hi> 5.13, 14, 15. <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 11.10. So that none entred into either of God's Rest but by him alone, who so testifieth by himself, <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> 5.39, 46. And by his Spirit, <ns0:hi>Acts</ns0:hi> 15.11.</ns0:note>: but the word <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Gr. <ns0:hi>The Word of hearing.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> preached did not profit them <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">The Gospel was so preached to them, that they did or might hear it, <ns0:hi>Rom.</ns0:hi> 10.14, 15. compare <ns0:hi>Psal<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g>
                     </ns0:hi> 92.4. <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 52.7. yet did it not prove effectual to many of those <ns0:hi>Hebrews</ns0:hi> to bring them either into the Literal or Heavenly <ns0:hi>Canaan,</ns0:hi> but came short of God's Rest in both; they not performing what he required; he by an irrever<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sible Sentence excluded them, see <ns0:hi>chap.</ns0:hi> 3.17, 19.</ns0:note>, not <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>because they were not united by Faith to.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> being mixed with faith in them that heard <ns0:hi>it</ns0:hi> 
                  <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>. A Metaphor taken from mixing things in the Stomach, as Meat and Drink, without the Concoction of which there can be no nourishing the Body, setting forth the Sin of these <ns0:hi>Hebrews,</ns0:hi> who never received nor mixed this Gospel which they heard with a sincere Faith in their Souls, so as being digested thereby, it might be united with it. Thus that which was the mighty Power and Wisdom of God to Salvation to those who believed, was a Word of Condemnation and Eternal Death to Unbelievers, 1 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 1.18. 1 <ns0:hi>Pet.</ns0:hi> 2.2, 3.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="3">3 For we which have believed do enter into rest <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">A further reason setting home this Counsel, was the certain benefit of our Care in Believing; for that the com<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />munity of real Christians, partakers and exercisers of the same precious Faith, as <ns0:hi>Paul</ns0:hi> himself, 2 <ns0:hi>Pet.</ns0:hi> 1.1. have the same priviledg as believing <ns0:hi>Caleb</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Ioshua</ns0:hi> had, <ns0:hi>Numb.</ns0:hi> 14.24, 30. to enter into God's Rest, initially having Peace with God now, and his Love shed abroad in their hearts by the Holy Ghost, witnessing their Reconciliation, Justifi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cation, Renovation, Adoption, so as they rejoice in Hope of the Glory of God, <ns0:hi>Rom.</ns0:hi> 5.1, 2, 5. and are by Believing and Obedience making out to the attainment of the final and compleat Rest of God in Heaven, of which they are afraid to fall short.</ns0:note>, as he said <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">God himself confirms this by his Oath, <ns0:hi>chap.</ns0:hi> 3.11, 18. <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 95.11. At the same time that he excludeth all Unbelievers from entring in, he inclusive<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ly and by consequence sweareth that all Believers do and shall enter in.</ns0:note>, As I have sworn in my wrath, If they shall enter into my rest <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">That Rest which <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi> there speaks of, was not God's Rest on the Seventh Day from the Creati<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />on after the finishing of God's Works, nor the Temporal Rest in the Land of <ns0:hi>Canaan,</ns0:hi> which the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> had and were past, as these <ns0:hi>Hebrews</ns0:hi> might suggest, but another. Rest to come, either in the World to come, <ns0:hi>chap.</ns0:hi> 2.5. or in the Heavenly Rest in Glory, which he takes occasion further to explain to them.</ns0:note>, although the works were finished from the foundation of the world <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> some render as a particle of exception <ns0:hi>although,</ns0:hi> as if it intended, <ns0:hi>although</ns0:hi> God's Rest is some-where meant of his Rest after the finishing of the Works of Creation, yet here God speaks of the Rest of <ns0:hi>Canaan</ns0:hi> a Type of the heavenly one; others, that God swore they should not enter into his Rest, <ns0:hi>although</ns0:hi> God's Works were done, and the Rest were ready, because of their Unbelief. Others render it, <ns0:hi>And indeed, he said and spake of the same hea<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />venly Rest,</ns0:hi> long before he spake of the Rest of <ns0:hi>Canaan, even upon the finishing of his Works from the foundation of the World</ns0:hi>; which seems most agreeable to the Spirit's Design here.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="4">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:550" />4 For he spake in a certain place of the se<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />venth <ns0:hi>day</ns0:hi> on this wise <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">The Spirit proves, that the Rest mentioned by <ns0:hi>David, Psal</ns0:hi> 95.11. is not meant the seventh days Rest, because spo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ken 3000 years after that Rest was past; but this Rest of which he speaks, was to come, tho spoken of, and known then: For <ns0:hi>Moses</ns0:hi> had spoken of it in a well-known place to them, <ns0:hi>Gen.</ns0:hi> 2.1, 2, 3. and this when he wrote of the seventh Day, which was eminently noting the Sabbath, and a Type of God's most excellent Rest which he sware unto Believers.</ns0:note>, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Exod. 31.17.</ns0:note> And god did rest the seventh day from all his works <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">God doth not here rest as if he were weary, <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 40.28. but ceased from the Creation of all kind of things he pur<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />posed to make, but not from their propagation and his pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vidence about them, <ns0:hi>Acts</ns0:hi> 17.25. And this he did on the se<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />venth Day, which he instituted a Sabbath for his People, <ns0:hi>Gen.</ns0:hi> 2.3. which resting-day may type out the eternal Rest of Angels and Men, when their Work of Obedience is finished: And yet was not God's Rest spoken of in the Psalm, nor pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mised in the Gospel to Believers, for this was yet to come; whereas the seventh Days Rest was entred into from the Foundation of the World.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="5">5 And in this <ns0:hi>place</ns0:hi> again <ns0:hi>o</ns0:hi>; If they shall enter into my rest <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Ei</ns0:hi> here is <ns0:hi>affirma<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tive,</ns0:hi> as appears by comp. <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 3. and 6. that these shall have a real and full possession in the future after <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi>'s time of this Rest, and therefore different from <ns0:hi>Moses</ns0:hi>'s Rest so long past before. The Word <ns0:hi>Rest</ns0:hi> in the Hebrew is not the same in the Text of <ns0:hi>Moses</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>David,</ns0:hi> Gen. 2.2, 3. it is <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>
in <ns0:hi>Psalm</ns0:hi> 95.11. <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> This of <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi> noting the full e<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />eternal, comfortable Rest of Souls in Glory, sworn by God to Believers in the Gospel.</ns0:note>.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> here is not so much <ns0:hi>copulative,</ns0:hi> connecting an Instance of <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi> to the same purpose of that of <ns0:hi>Moses</ns0:hi> about the seventh Days Rest from the Creation, but <ns0:hi>discretive,</ns0:hi> joyning an Instance of another Rest of God different from the seventh Days Rest. <ns0:hi>Moses</ns0:hi> spake of this, but <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi> here of a further Rest; for in <ns0:hi>Psalm</ns0:hi> 95.11. <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi> spake not of the seventh Day, but of God's last and eternal Rest.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="6">6 Seeing therefore it remaineth that some must enter therein <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">The Spirit having demonstrated, that God's Rest sworn to Believers in the Gospel, and mentioned by <ns0:hi>David,</ns0:hi> could not be the seventh Days Rest; proceeds to prove likewise, that it could not be the Rest of <ns0:hi>Israel</ns0:hi> in the Land of <ns0:hi>Canaan,</ns0:hi> since that was entred into 400 years before he wrote by the Spirit of this better Rest, since those unbelieving <ns0:hi>Israel</ns0:hi> that entred into <ns0:hi>Canaan</ns0:hi> never entred into this Rest. Forasmuch then as a Rest to come is spoken of, and that some Believers must have a real and full possession of the glorious Rest of<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fered to them in the Gospel, as <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi> foretold; see <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 9.10, 11.</ns0:note>, and they to whom <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>the Gospel was first preach<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> it was first preached, entred not in because of un<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />belief <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">The unbelieving <ns0:hi>Israel</ns0:hi> who had the glad Tidings of this Rest preached unto them by <ns0:hi>Moses</ns0:hi> and by <ns0:hi>David,</ns0:hi> &c. yet entred not into it, tho they entred into, and lived in <ns0:hi>Canaan,</ns0:hi> because of their Disobedience and Unbelief. Then it follows <ns0:hi>Canaan</ns0:hi>'s Rest and this cannot be all one; and the latter is only intended by <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi> here.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="7">7 Again, he limiteth a certain day, saying in David <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">This is a further Proof, that <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi> did not mean or intend the rest of the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> in <ns0:hi>Canaan,</ns0:hi> in the 95th Psalm, from the determined time of it; as if the Spirit had said, besides what I have proved, take another Argument; <ns0:hi>Again I argue.</ns0:hi> God by the Prophet setteth out, and severeth from all other Time a <ns0:hi>certain stated Day,</ns0:hi> from which the Rest spoken of, is cleared, and of it testifieth by him, <ns0:hi>Psalm</ns0:hi> 95.7, 8.</ns0:note>, To day, after so long a time <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">After 400 Years past of <ns0:hi>Israel</ns0:hi>'s Rest in <ns0:hi>Canaan,</ns0:hi> which was a long Time, doth <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi> say <ns0:hi>of to day,</ns0:hi> a Time present, then and further to be extended, even the Gospel-day, in <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi>'s Time, and after it, not in <ns0:hi>Ioshua</ns0:hi>'s, for that was past long before.</ns0:note>; as it is said, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 3.7.</ns0:note> To day, if ye will hear his voice, har<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />den not your hearts <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">Ye ought <ns0:hi>to day</ns0:hi> to hear, receive, and believe the Gospel of God's Rest, and not by Unbelief to turn your Hearts from the Voice of God in the Gospel.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="8">8 For if <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">That is, <ns0:hi>Io<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />
                        <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="4 letters">
                           <ns0:desc>••••</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> Jesus had given them rest <ns0:note n="w" place="bottom">This is the Improvement of the former instance, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 7. If <ns0:hi>Ioshua</ns0:hi> by bringing <ns0:hi>Israel</ns0:hi> into <ns0:hi>Canaan,</ns0:hi> had given rest to all Believers, then God would not by <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi> have spoken of ano<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther Day and State of Rest to come. <ns0:hi>Ioshua</ns0:hi> was, <ns0:hi>Acts</ns0:hi> 7.45. a Type of Jesus bringing Believers into the true Rest of the heavenly <ns0:hi>Canaan,</ns0:hi> as he did <ns0:hi>Israel</ns0:hi> into a literal one. If that of <ns0:hi>Canaan</ns0:hi> was the full, and perfect Rest of Believers, which was given them by him.</ns0:note>, then would he not afterward have spoken of another day <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">Then God himself would not have spoke by <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi> of a better and heavenly Rest promised Believers in the Gospel; of which spiritual and eternal one, both God's seventh-day Sabbath, and the Rest of <ns0:hi>Canaan</ns0:hi> were but fainter Shadows & Types. The Expostulation is vehemently denying it.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="9">9 There remaineth therefore a <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>keeping of a Sabbath.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> rest to the people of God <ns0:note n="y" place="bottom">Here the Spirit concludes from his former Proofs, That there is a more excellent Rest revealed to Faith in the Go<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />spel, which is remaining, future, and to come, and will sure, and most certainly do so; tho it be behind, yet it will be enjoyed. A Sabbatism, which is a State and Season a of most glorious Rest, see <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 10. shall be enjoyed by sincere Belie<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vers, the true <ns0:hi>Israel</ns0:hi> of God, of whom he is the Proprietor, and who are for their eternal State so excellently holy, and of so divine a Nature, that he is not ashamed to be called their God. They have an Entrance here into the initials of this Sabbatism in internal Peace, and the glorious Liberty of the Children of God; and by it secured of their full Pos<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />session of it in the eternal Inheritance of the Saints in Light. <ns0:hi>Colos.</ns0:hi> 1.12, 13. 1 <ns0:hi>Pet.</ns0:hi> 1.3, 4, 5. <ns0:hi>Rev.</ns0:hi> 14.13.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="10">10 For he that is entred into his rest <ns0:note n="z" place="bottom">This proveth the foregoing Consequence of a <ns0:hi>Rest re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />maining,</ns0:hi> from the Nature of a true Rest, which is a resting from all Labours, which the <ns0:hi>Israelites</ns0:hi> did not in <ns0:hi>Canaan,</ns0:hi> therefore it is yet to come. For every true Believer who hath full possession of God's Rest; where God is satisfying of them in bliss, they rest in his Loves, of which the Sabbath and <ns0:hi>Ca<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />naan</ns0:hi> were but Types.</ns0:note>, he al<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />so hath ceased from his own works <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">Such true Christians have ceased and rested from all their sinful Works and Labours, as Works of Callings, Miseries, Anxieties, and Sufferings of any kind, resting from them perfectly and perpetually, having finished all his Work of Evangelical Obedience through them.</ns0:note>, as God <ns0:hi>did</ns0:hi> from his <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">They have rested not in a <ns0:hi>Parity</ns0:hi> of <ns0:hi>Rest, or Work in kind,</ns0:hi> but as God from his own <ns0:hi>in likeness of order,</ns0:hi> his Work going before Rest, and of Rest fitted for<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> Believers by him conformable to his own. Some refer these Words and the Relative <ns0:hi>he</ns0:hi> to our Lord Je<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sus Christ, as Head of his Body the Church of true Belie<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lievers; and that the Parallel runs between God the Father and him in the Works of the Old and New Creation, which Works were good and compleat in their different Kinds in their Cessation from them, and their Rest in their respective Sabbaths; both Days being founded thereon; and that Be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lievers shall be conformable to their Head, treading in his steps, in doing and suffering, and then in Rest.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="11">11 Let us labour therefore to enter into that rest <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">This is the Use of the former Doctrine, that since many through Unbelief fall short of God's Rest, therefore let us la<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bour. <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> imports Study of Mind, Earnestness of Affection, Diligence of Endeavour, with all the Powers of Soul and Body to intend this Work: so is it used, 2 <ns0:hi>Pet.</ns0:hi> 1.10. This is the most necessary, excellent, and important one to us in this World, our single great Business in it; and there<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fore as Students our Minds must be bent on it, and our Wills fixed and resolved about it, and the Operations of all the exe<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cutive Powers of our Persons put forth to the utmost Degree, so as all the Duties necessary thereunto, as Attendance on all Ordinances, and the constant Exercise of Faith and Obedi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ence, must be fitting us for, and bringing us into the full pos<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />session of the eternally blessed and glorious Rest of God, 2 <ns0:hi>Pet.</ns0:hi> 1.5 to 12.</ns0:note>, lest any man fall after the same ex<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ample of <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>disobedi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ence.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> unbelief <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">That not any particular Person may fall into sin and the Consequents of it; the Particle <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> may be read <ns0:hi>into,</ns0:hi> and then it implies, lest any of you prove Rebels and Apostates. Or, it is read <ns0:hi>by,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>after,</ns0:hi> and then it is a Fall to Destruction and Hell, with all the Miseries that those feel who are shut out of God's Rest, as their unbelieving Forefa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />thers were. God spared neither Apostate Men nor Angels, and will not spare others if they sin as those did. Our Judgments may be rather sorer, being warned by their Ex<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ample, 1 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 10.11. comp. <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> 10.26, 27, 29. They were contumacious and disobeyed the Gospel of God's Rest, there<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fore he destoryed them in the Wilderness, and thrust them down to Hell for ever: Avoid you their Sin, as you would la<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bour to avoid their Punishment.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="12">12 For the Word of God <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">The Efficacy of the Word of God is a further Inforce<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ment of their studious Labour to enter into God's Rest; for that calleth us thereunto, even the Law and Doctrine of the Gospel brought by the <ns0:hi>Incarnate Word</ns0:hi> from Heaven, preached by him to the World, dictated and inspired into the holy Pen<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />men both of the Old and New-Testament by the Holy Ghost, and written by them at his Call and Order, 2 <ns0:hi>Pet.</ns0:hi> 1.19, 20, 21. representing all those Precepts and Prohibitions, Promi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ses and Threatnings by which God will judge to whom this Gospel hath been preached in that Man whom he hath ap<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pointed. Compare <ns0:hi>ch.</ns0:hi> 2.1, 2. and <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 1, 2. of this.                         <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>, not only a <ns0:hi>living</ns0:hi> Word, but a <ns0:hi>quickning Word,</ns0:hi> making dead Sinners living Christians; Souls dead in Sins and Trespasses, alive to God. This Word, the Breath of God, conveyeth Spirit and Life to them, 2 <ns0:hi>Tim.</ns0:hi> 3.16. 1 <ns0:hi>Pet.</ns0:hi> 1.23. so <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi> experi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />enced it, preserving the Life it breathed into him, <ns0:hi>Psalm</ns0:hi> 119.50. and the Members of the Church, 1 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 4.15. comp. 2 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 3.6, 17, 18. and as a Rule it guideth and directeth them through Christ unto eternal Life, <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> 6.68.</ns0:note> and powerful <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>, it's an <ns0:hi>active Word,</ns0:hi> powerful in its Effects, the very Mi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nistration of the Spirit, 2 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 3.8. most efficacious and ener<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />getical for convincing, converting, comforting; and for con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />demning, killing: It acts like the Power of God; so <ns0:hi>Rom.</ns0:hi> 1.16, 18.</ns0:note>, and sharper than any <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">Rev. 1.16.</ns0:note> two-edged sword <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> signifieth <ns0:hi>a cutting Sharpness</ns0:hi> as be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cometh several Uses, as searching, letting out Corruption, or for killing; all which agree to this Divine Word; sharper than any <ns0:hi>Sword with two Mouths.</ns0:hi> The <ns0:hi>Hebrews</ns0:hi> stile the <ns0:hi>Edge</ns0:hi> the <ns0:hi>Mouth,</ns0:hi> that which bites, teareth, or woundeth; as <ns0:hi>Rev.</ns0:hi> 1.16. and 2.12. So is it used, <ns0:hi>Ephes.</ns0:hi> 6.17. comp. <ns0:hi>Acts</ns0:hi> 2.37. and 7.54. It is Christ's Weapon of Offence and Defence for his People, and it cuts without Resistance; with it he is defending his Truth, and smiting his Enemies, <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 11.4. comp. <ns0:hi>Rev.</ns0:hi> 19.13, 15, 21.</ns0:note>, piercing even to the dividing asunder <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:gap reason="foreign">

                     <ns0:gap reason="foreign">

                     </ns0:gap> the Soul of Man regenerate and spiritualiz'd, called Spirit, 1 <ns0:hi>Thess.</ns0:hi> 5.23. The Soul inlightned, renewed, and governed by the Holy Ghost, not altered as to its Sub<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stance, but as to its Qualities, whose Understanding, Will and Affections are spiritualiz'd, manifested in its Actions a<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />greeable to the spiritual Will of God, 1 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 2.10, 12, 14, 15. These are both of them under the piercing Power of the Word, and the Spirit can reach them by it as he pleaseth.</ns0:note>, and of the joints and mar<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />row <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> are not the Members, but the <ns0:hi>Nerves, Membranes, Muscles,</ns0:hi> whereby the Members or Limbs are joyn<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed one to another, so as not without Incision to de discovered, and <ns0:hi>the Marrow</ns0:hi> within the Bones, there must be a breaking or perforating them to reach it. By which Metaphors are set out the <ns0:hi>hardest, compactest,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>most intimate Parts of a Sin<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ner, the most secret hidden ones,</ns0:hi> which no natural Reason can reach, yet the Word of God pierceth them, to discover either the evil or good of them, and to inflict Wrath, or communi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cate Comfort according to their Conditions.</ns0:note>, and <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> a discerner of the thoughts and intents of the heart <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">The Word of God <ns0:hi>is a most nice, exact, and critical Iudge,</ns0:hi> discerning the Gravity and Rectitude of them; it discovers and distinguish<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />eth them as they are, or not agreeable to it self, the funda<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mental Truth; and is capable, as a Judge, to charge or dis<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />charge as its Author will, by it. <ns0:hi>Rom.</ns0:hi> 2.12, 15, 16. compare 1 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 14.24, 25. It discovers the most inward, close, se<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cret and constant Motions, both speculative and practical, of the Soul of Man inseparably united to the Heart, and one with another, whether they are Opinions, Conceptions, Re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />solutions, or Decrees, so subtile and so secret, as who can know them, but who made the Heart, <ns0:hi>Gen.</ns0:hi> 6.5. <ns0:hi>Ier.</ns0:hi> 17.9.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>

                     </ns0:gap>, 12.</ns0:note> Neither is there any creature that is not manifest in his sight <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">

                     </ns0:gap> is not only <ns0:hi>copulative,</ns0:hi> but <ns0:hi>rational,</ns0:hi> shewing the ground of the former Efficacy of the <ns0:hi>Gospel-Word,</ns0:hi> because its Au<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />thor seeth and knoweth all Persons and Things, and filleth it with this power and Force. For every Creature which God the Son created, Angel, or Man, or any other, from the greatest to the least, from the Leviathan to a Mite, and all parts of every Creature, especially of every Creature to whom the Gospel is preached, <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> 16.15. not any one is <ns0:gap reason="foreign">

                     <ns0:hi>without light,</ns0:hi> invisible, unapparent, obscure, or possible to be covered, or hid, or concealed from his View or Face; where the Relative <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> agreeth with <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>

                     </ns0:gap>, or <ns0:hi>the Word, v.</ns0:hi> 12. as the following Relative e<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vinceth. To this God-Man no Spirit nor Thought can be hid; it shall not be so from the efficacious Power of his Word, much less shall Infidelity or Hypocrisie be hid from it, or his most piercing Eye.</ns0:note>: but all things <ns0:hi>are</ns0:hi> naked and opened <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">But all <ns0:hi>things</ns0:hi> in general and particular, not any one excepted, is <ns0:hi>bare, naked, uncloathed,</ns0:hi> the Covering is removed, all Secrets are open and manifest to view, God the Son seeth within and without, all are unveiled to him, and <ns0:hi>laid open as by Dissection.</ns0:hi> 
                     <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>

a Metaphor taken from the sacrificed Beasts, which be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing skinned, were cut open from the Neck, and so divided by the Chine to the Rump, or by the Throat downward im<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bowelled by the Priests, so as every part within may be clear<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ly seen whether clean or unclean. The Truth of which is, that every thing in the World, even the most secret and inward Thoughts of the Heart of a Sinner, which is a great Deep, is opened and laid forth to every Scruple unto God in Christ; every secret Unbelief, apostatizing Principle, or Hy<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pocrisie he discerneth clearly and fully, <ns0:hi>Ier.</ns0:hi> 17.9, 10. he that made the Eye, must see best.</ns0:note> to the eyes of him with whom we have to do <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">His Eyes who pierceth be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />yond the Vultures into things and places that no Eye can di<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />scern, the Souls of Men, <ns0:hi>Iob</ns0:hi> 28.7, 10. <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 94.9. <ns0:hi>Prov.</ns0:hi> 20.12. All this is asserted concerning the Person of whom <ns0:hi>Paul</ns0:hi> writes, <ns0:hi>Christ God-Man,</ns0:hi> the great Gospel-Minister, whose Word is so powerfully piercing: Of him and his Word is all this Speech and Discourse; he it is who is the All-knowing and impartial Judge, and makes his Gospel Word of Counsel, Promise, and Threatnings to cut so deeply, and search the secrets of the Hearts of all.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="14">14 Seeing then that we have a great high priest <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">The excellency of the great <ns0:hi>Gospel-Minister</ns0:hi> beyond all others in respect of his <ns0:hi>Priestly Office,</ns0:hi> especially beyond <ns0:hi>Aaron</ns0:hi> and the Levitical Priesthood, is shewn by the Holy Ghost from this Verse to Chap. 5. <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 11. It is introduced, as the Spirits counsel to these Hebrews, from the Premises for their using of this High Priest, in order to their reaching home to the Rest of God, to whom and whose Profession they ought to adhere, since he is so fit, and so willing to give them an entrance into it, comp. <ns0:hi>chap.</ns0:hi> 2.17, 18. and 3.1, 6. Being therefore by the Spirit through Faith not only interested by a common Relation in him, but by a real Union to, and Com<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />munion with him, as here described an High Priest, <ns0:hi>ch.</ns0:hi> 2.11. and 3.1. so great as none was, or can equal him. All the High Priests on earth but imperfect Types of him; above <ns0:hi>Aaron</ns0:hi> and all others; the grand Presider over all God's Worship, who had Work peculiar to himself above all: The Supreme and Universal Priest in Heaven and Earth, whose Title the <ns0:hi>Roman</ns0:hi> Antichrist usurpeth; to him only due, <ns0:hi>Pontifex optimus maximus,</ns0:hi> yet officiating always for us.</ns0:note>, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 7.26. & 9.12.</ns0:note> that is passed into the heavens <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">He hath fulfilled his Type, entring into the Holy of Holiest in Heaven, taking Possession of God's Rest, and purchasing an Entrance for us into it, and this after the removal of the Curse, satisfaction of the Divine Justice for our Sins, Victory over all Enemies that would oppose his or our Entrance by him, as Sin, Wrath, Death, and the Devil, and keeping possession of this Rest for us, <ns0:hi>ch.</ns0:hi> 9.23, 24, and 28.</ns0:note>; Jesus the son of God <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Iesus</ns0:hi> the Saviour of his People from all their Sins, their Emmanuel, <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 1.20, 21, 23. who being God the Son by eternal Generation, was incarnate by taking to himself and uniting a true Body and a reasonable Soul, being conceived miraculously by the Virgin <ns0:hi>Mary</ns0:hi> from the overshadowing of the Holy Ghost; in which Nature, inseparably united to his Person, he fulfilled all Righteousness, and died a Sacrifice for our Sins, and rose in our Nature, and ascended and entred into the Holy of Ho<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />liest in Heaven, and made Atonement, and laid open the way to Believers to enter God's Rest there.</ns0:note>, <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">Chap. 10.23.</ns0:note> let us hold fast <ns0:hi>our</ns0:hi> profes<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sion <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">The intire Reli<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gion of which Jesus is the Author, as opposite to that of the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> in its Principles and practick part of it, <ns0:hi>ch.</ns0:hi> 3.1. is powerfully, strongly, and perseveringly to be held by his without Relaxation, in which if we follow him, cleave to him, and by him labour to enter, we shall not come short of God's Rest, <ns0:hi>ch.</ns0:hi> 7.24, 25. where the Head is, there shall the Body be also, <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> 14.2, 3. and 17.24.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="15">15 For <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 2.18.</ns0:note> we have not an high priest, which cannot be touched with the feeling of our infir<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mities <ns0:note n="w" place="bottom">This Duty of perseverance in the Christian Religion, is inforced by the Consideration of the Sympathy of this High-Priest, with the States of all who will enter into God's Rest by him. He is worthy that we should hold it fast, being with<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />out impotency. It is impossible he should be pitiless to peni<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tent Sinners, tho he be glorious, there being nothing in him<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />self, or out of himself indisposing him to it. <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>
imports such a Sympathy or Fellow-feeling, as makes him like affected as if he were in the same case with them. He can<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />not but be compassionate, since inwardly affected and moved with the Sufferings of his, <ns0:hi>Acts</ns0:hi> 9.5. comp. <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 63.9. As God, he is infinitely merciful; as Man, inwardly feeling them<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> even all the Miseries they were liable to, but sinful ones. He wants no Bowels, but he hath as a fellow-feeling, so a fellow-grieving, and fellow-caring for the Redress of them, even all such as are fit for his Pity; and works on Affections, a sense of Guilt, Fears, Doubts, Tremblings, Weak-workings to God, the concomitant Infirmities of sinful Souls; all the Weaknesses of Grace in us, all Troubles, Distresses, An<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />guishes in the Flesh, the Fruits of Sin. He knows these <ns0:hi>sensibly</ns0:hi> as Man, which as God singly he could not. These sinful weak<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nesses of Soul inclining to sin, and disabling from resisting Temptations by which the subtil powerful Enemy of our Soul prevaileth over us to the Accumulating of Sin and Guilt daily, and so need this Sympathy of his to us-ward; see <ns0:hi>ch.</ns0:hi> 5.2. 1 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 2.3. 2 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 11.23 to 31. and 12.5, 9, 10.</ns0:note>, <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">Luke 22.28.</ns0:note> but was in all points tempted like as we are, <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">2 Cor. 5.21.</ns0:note> 
                  <ns0:hi>yet</ns0:hi> without sin <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">But <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> was pierced and tried by all sorts of Sufferings being outwardly tempted by the Devil to sin; inwardly he could not, being perfectly holy, <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> 14.30. but was outwardly with Violence assaulted by him, <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 4.1, to 12. and tried by Men beyond any Man, and tempted to the same Sins whereby <ns0:hi>Adam</ns0:hi> fell, and others miscarry every Day. He felt the Curse of Sin, the Wrath of God, Agonies in his Soul, violent pains in his Body, Sorrows to the Death from the Cradle to the Cross: And in every <ns0:hi>matter of Grief and Suffering</ns0:hi> in Soul, in Body, from the World, from Satan, from God, in all kind of Temptations spiritual and temporal; experiencing the Evils of this Life, Hunger, Thirst, Weari<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ness, Grief, <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 53.3, to 11. even such as <ns0:hi>we are</ns0:hi> liable to, all of them really and truly like ours, and more powerfully than ours; they were for similitude like, but for Degree exceed<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing them; ours for Exquisiteness of Sense, but a shadow of his: Yet under all these Temptations he was <ns0:hi>sinless</ns0:hi> as the Holy One of God; never did Temptation prevail over him, he overcame all. Nothing was out of place or order by his Sufferings in him: All his Affections and Passions under these, regular, shewing his Innocency under variety of Sufferings and eminency of Compassions. Sin hardens Bowels, but he is compassionate without any mixture with, or hinderance by Corruption; and his Intercession is the more effectual with God for us. What Christian under his Conduct would not follow his great Example, so to resist and conquer by him?</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="16">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:551" />16 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 10.19, 21, 22.</ns0:note> Let us therefore come boldly unto the throne of grace <ns0:note n="y" place="bottom">Since our High Priest hath a sense of our Infirmities, hath experienced our Tryals, and no Sin is in him to shut up his Bowels of Compassion, therefore haste we to him, as those who desire to reach Favours from our Soveraign, as our poor, guilty, needy Souls want them. It is a <ns0:hi>Soul-motion</ns0:hi> by Faith and Love breathed forth in strong Cries to his God and Father and ours, constantly approaching God in every Duty by him. comp. <ns0:hi>chap.</ns0:hi> 10.19 to <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 23. and that with <ns0:hi>open Face, boldness and assurance,</ns0:hi> without any shame or dismay, coming in the Name, and with the person of our great High Priest, who takes our duties and persons, and presents them per<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fumed with the Incense of his Merits to him. Away now with all Unbelief, Doubtings, or Fears in our approach to him; Admission to him, and hearing by him is now certain unto the Believer, <ns0:hi>Rom.</ns0:hi> 5.1, 2. <ns0:hi>Ephes.</ns0:hi> 2.18. and 3.12. 1 <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> 3.21, 22. and 5.14, 15. For his Throne, now the Father is propitiated by him, is from a Throne of strict Ju<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stice made a Throne of Grace, of which the propitiatory Seat over the Ark of the Covenant in the Holy of Holiest both in the Tabernacle and Temple was a Type. All the Terror and Dread of it is now done away by Christ. Thun<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />derings, and Lightnings, and Voices, and the sound of a Trum<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pet are now ceased; the still Voice of pardon, peace, pur<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ging and saving Sinners proceeds from it; Grace in refe<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rence to Believers sits in all its Glory, and Majesty, and Power only, <ns0:hi>Rev.</ns0:hi> 5.1, 6, 13. comp. <ns0:hi>ch.</ns0:hi> 8.1. and 12.2. <ns0:hi>Ephes.</ns0:hi> 1.20. Christ now takes us by the hand, brings us thither, and pleads by his own Blood for us, so as we may approach to it with greatest confidence.</ns0:note>, that we may obtain mercy, and find grace to help in time of need <ns0:note n="z" place="bottom">That we may actually partake of the Fruits of Christ's purchase and intercession from the Father of Mercy, pity suitable to our misery, pardon for our guilty Souls, and relief for us under all our Afflictions, <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 63.7, 8, 9. and all Grace necessary for us at all times for a seasonable help, but especially in times of greatest need: <ns0:hi>It is most opportune, when most helpful</ns0:hi>; when Infirmities, Afflictions, Temptations, and the Snares of Sin beset us with grievous persecutions, then may we by Prayer, through our High Priest, have recourse to this Throne of Grace for our sutable and sufficient supply, without which there is no hold<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing fast our profession, or possibility of entrance into God's Rest.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
